text: Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds Check shallow-water bed sources and hydrostatic reconstruction with wet/emerged lakes and a SWASHES steady Bernoulli flow. A separate flat-bed Ritter dam break tests genuinely dry states, conservation budgets and a fixed-depth front. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-shallow-water-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. SWASHES topographic flow: lakes and nonzero steady discharge Check two lake equilibria separately from nonzero subcritical flow, distinguishing lake preservation from moving-flow discretization error. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries 1D, g=9.81, L=25m, compact parabolic bed z=.2-.05(x-10)^2 on8<x<12. Lakes at surface .5/.1m use200 cells. Moving flow q=4.42m2/s, downstream h=2m uses100/200/400 cells to2s. Initialize the steady branch, not the published rest-to-steady transient. Editorial clarification Exact lake balance concerns the represented cell bed. Moving steady states retain finite-time numerical error. Transcritical flows, jumps, friction, rain, infiltration, 2D flow and fully discrete entropy stability are outside scope. The final revision passed31 unit checks and all109 gates over8 group runs. The finest moving steady case,N400, has depthL1 about.0249108 and relative depthL1 about.000505933. Represented-bed lake balance, finite-time moving steady errors and dry-bed front errors are retained separately. Adopted numerical method Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Dry-bed dam break: actual wetting and dry states Start the right half at exactly h=q=0 and compare wetting-front advance, conservation and conservative errors with the Ritter analytic solution. Methods, equations, figures and references Input and validation protocol history · Initial input Assumptions, units and boundaries Flat frictionless bed on[-10,10]m, dam0, hL=1m/hR=0, initial velocity0, g=9.81, t=.5s,1600/3200/6400 cells. The Ritter formula uses an explicit rescaling distinct from the paper numerical example. Editorial clarification The .001m mean-depth contour differs from the analytic support edge, which is reported separately. These fixed runs test wetting of initially dry cells. Retreating shorelines, re-drying cycles, real floods, friction and moving fronts over topography are outside scope. The initial100/200/400-cell [-5,5]m attempt passed28 tests and105/109 gates; three retained-dry-cell gates and the .3960m>.25m contour error failed. All original records remain archived; revision2 enlarges/refines the input without changing acceptance. Revision2 then stopped on a binary64 subnormal-tail dry-momentum artifact. Revision3 factors the same HLL update into water packets and adds three regression/equivalence tests; the original28 remain unchanged. Revision3 passed108/109 gates but failed the .27415m>.25m contour criterion. Revision4 refines only Ritter grids to1600/3200/6400. Relative depth L1 is normalized by domain reference mass; absolute L1 is also retained because the domain changed between revisions1 and2. Final revision4 uses1600/3200/6400cells on[-10,10]m at t.5s and passed31 unit checks and all109 group gates. Acceptance depthL1 retains the original fixed reference mass5m², giving finest.001773819 and absolute depthL1.008869095m². Normalization by the enlarged-domain reference mass10m² gives.000886909 as a separate diagnostic, never an easier acceptance criterion. Relative momentumL1 is.009590172; the depth.001m contour error is.2069613m<.25m and1679 genuinely dry cells remain. All three earlier failures are retained; depth floors,state clips and retries are zero. Adopted numerical method The FV solver supports h=q=0 directly; one-sided dry HLL speeds use u-c/u+2c and their reflection. Forward Euler at face CFL .4 records every minimum and shared-flux budget without raising cell depths.
